evals.prompt: babysit PR #42 — watch it until it's merged or I need to take action
evals.expected_output: Skill enters Watch mode: resolves PR #42, runs fetch-pr-state.sh, enters monitoring loop polling CI every 60s, surfaces CI failures with classification (branch-related vs flaky), surfaces human review comments for user approval before replying, emits one-time 'CI green, watching…' update when all checks pass, and stops only when PR is merged/closed or user intervention is required.
expectations: Resolves the PR number (42) and fetches initial state via fetch-pr-state.sh or gh pr view
Enters a monitoring loop rather than checking once and stopping
Correctly identifies Watch mode (not Drive mode) from the user's intent
Does not attempt to post review replies without explicit user approval
Classifies any CI failures as branch-related, flaky, or unrelated before taking action
Reports state changes (not every poll) — e.g. 'CI is green (N/N checks). Watching for review comments.'
Does not merge without explicit user approval

evals.prompt: drive PR #7 to merge — address all review comments and merge it when ready
evals.expected_output: Skill enters Drive mode: fetches PR state, iterates through unresolved review threads (using resolve-thread.sh and review-reply.md.tmpl for canonical replies), fixes related code, pushes commits, monitors CI until green, validates all merge readiness conditions (green CI, 0 unresolved threads, up-to-date with base), prints 'PR is ready for your approval. Reply `approved` to merge.' and waits — does NOT merge until the user writes 'approved'.
expectations: Resolves the PR number (7) and detects Drive mode from 'drive' and 'merge' intent
Uses fetch-pr-state.sh to get unresolved review threads
Addresses each unresolved review thread using agree/partially-agree/disagree shapes from templates/review-reply.md.tmpl
Uses resolve-thread.sh to mark threads resolved after replying
Pushes any code fixes without [skip ci] prefix in commit message
Restarts monitoring loop after pushing fixes, does not stop at push
Prints the explicit merge-approval gate message before merging
Does not call gh pr merge before receiving 'approved' from the user
Calls cleanup-after-merge.sh after merging

evals.prompt: watch my PR, CI keeps failing — it's PR #99 in the myorg/backend repo
evals.expected_output: Skill resolves PR #99, fetches logs for the failing CI run via gh run view --log-failed, classifies the failure (branch-related patch vs. flaky/infra retry vs. unrelated escalation), takes the appropriate action (patch+push, or gh run rerun --failed up to 3×, or stop for user), then resumes monitoring. Does not change CI config or test files unless logs clearly connect to the PR branch.
expectations: Identifies and fetches the failing CI run ID using gh run list filtered to the PR's commit SHA
Fetches failure logs via gh run view --log-failed or gh api check-runs
Classifies the failure as branch-related, flaky/infra, unrelated, or ambiguous
For flaky failures: retries with gh run rerun --failed (max 3 attempts), not by modifying code
For branch-related failures: patches the file, commits without [skip ci], pushes, and restarts monitoring
For unrelated failures: reports to user and stops rather than silently waiting
Does not modify CI YAML or test files to silence a flaky test

evals.prompt: babysit PR #15 — it has a merge conflict, fix it and then watch CI
evals.expected_output: Skill detects mergeable=CONFLICTING on PR #15, identifies the conflicting files, rebases the PR branch onto the base branch using git rebase with --force-with-lease push, restarts the monitoring loop after the push (triggering a new CI run), and then continues watching CI and review comments. Does not auto-resolve conflicts in files the PR did not touch — surfaces those to the user.
expectations: Detects mergeable=CONFLICTING via fetch-pr-state.sh or gh pr view before entering the standard loop
Uses git rebase (not git merge) to resolve the conflict, keeping history clean
Pushes the resolved branch with --force-with-lease, not a bare --force
Restarts the monitoring loop after pushing the rebase — does not stop at conflict resolution
Does not auto-resolve conflicts in files the PR did not touch; surfaces those to the user for manual resolution
Does not use gh pr merge --admin to bypass the conflict

evals.prompt: watch PR #33 — the CI keeps failing with runner provisioning errors, retry until it passes
evals.expected_output: Skill identifies the failing CI run as a flaky/infra failure (runner provisioning error in logs), retries with gh run rerun --failed up to 3 times. After the 3rd retry still fails, it stops retrying, reports the check name and a summary of the last log output, states that manual investigation is needed, and does NOT attempt a 4th retry or modify CI config/tests.
expectations: Fetches the failing run ID and logs via gh run view --log-failed
Classifies the failure as flaky/infra (not branch-related) based on 'runner provisioning' signal in logs
Retries exactly 3 times with gh run rerun --failed; does not retry a 4th time
After exhausting retries, reports the check name and last log summary to the user
Does not modify CI YAML, test files, or dependency pins to suppress the flaky runner
Suggests manual investigation (e.g., GitHub Actions support) rather than finding a workaround

evals.prompt: babysit PR #8 — it was reviewed by both alice and bob, address all their comments
evals.expected_output: Skill enters Drive mode, fetches all unresolved review threads (from both alice and bob), groups them by reviewer, addresses each thread using the agree/partially-agree/disagree shapes from templates/review-reply.md.tmpl, batches code fixes into one commit, pushes once, resolves each thread with resolve-thread.sh, then re-fetches state to confirm 0 unresolved threads remain. If alice and bob left conflicting opinions on the same line, skill surfaces the conflict to the user rather than silently picking one reviewer's side.
expectations: Fetches review threads from ALL reviewers (alice AND bob), not just the first one
Groups unresolved threads by reviewer in its status update
Uses review-reply.md.tmpl shapes (agree/partially-agree/disagree) for each thread reply
Batches code fixes from multiple threads into a single commit rather than one commit per thread
Calls resolve-thread.sh for each resolved thread after replying
Re-fetches PR state after pushing to confirm 0 unresolved threads (handles new threads added mid-fix)
Surfaces conflicting reviewer opinions to the user instead of silently choosing one
